items.title: Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center Software Authentication Bypass Vulnerability
items.one_liner: Critical authentication bypass vulnerability in Cisco Secure FMC allows unauthenticated remote attackers to gain root access.
items.summary: A vulnerability in the web interface of Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center (FMC) Software allows unauthenticated, remote attackers to bypass authentication and execute script files to gain root access to the underlying operating system. The flaw stems from an improper system process created at boot time and can be exploited by sending crafted HTTP requests. Cisco has released software updates to address the issue with no workarounds available. The attack surface is minimized if the management interface lacks public internet access.
key_facts: Vulnerable product: Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center Software
Impact: Authentication bypass and root access
items.bottom_line: Administrators must immediately apply Cisco software updates to secure vulnerable Firewall Management Center installations against root compromise.

items.title: CVE-2026-42018: JFrog JFrog Artifactory Improper Authentication Vulnerability
items.one_liner: JFrog Artifactory has an authentication bypass bug actively tracked by CISA that leaks internal tokens even when anonymous access is disabled.
items.summary: CISA has listed CVE-2026-42018 in its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, covering an improper authentication flaw in JFrog Artifactory. The bug allows an unauthenticated caller to receive an internal anonymous-user token even when anonymous access is explicitly disabled, potentially exposing sensitive repository assets. CISA has mandated that federal agencies apply vendor mitigations or discontinue using the software by September 25, 2026.
items.bottom_line: Audit JFrog Artifactory deployments and apply patches immediately to prevent unauthorized access to internal artifact tokens.

items.title: ZDI-26-645: Fortinet FortiSandbox write_remote_backup_to_crontab cronValue Command Injection Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
items.one_liner: Authenticated attackers can gain root-level code execution on your FortiSandbox appliances.
items.summary: Fortinet has patched a critical command injection vulnerability in FortiSandbox, tracked as ZDI-26-645. The flaw exists in the write_remote_backup_to_crontab endpoint, where the cronValue parameter is not properly validated before being used in a system call. An authenticated attacker can exploit this to execute arbitrary code with root privileges.

items.title: CVE-2026-87491: Google Google Chromium V8 Out of Bounds Write Vulnerability
items.one_liner: Chromium's V8 engine has an exploited out-of-bounds write vulnerability requiring immediate browser patching across enterprise environments.
items.summary: CISA has added CVE-2026-87491 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The flaw is an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in Google Chromium's V8 engine that allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code within the sandbox using a specially crafted HTML page. It impacts Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Opera, and other Chromium-based browsers. Federal agencies have been instructed to remediate or mitigate the flaw by September 23, 2026, pursuant to BOD 26-04 guidelines.
items.bottom_line: Update all Chromium-based browsers immediately to patch an actively exploited V8 engine vulnerability.

items.title: BlueMoon Exploit Kit Chains Recent Chrome, Windows Zero-Days
items.one_liner: Chinese espionage groups are chaining Chrome and Windows zero-days via the BlueMoon exploit kit to target aerospace, NGOs, and governments.
items.summary: Proofpoint disclosed that multiple state-sponsored Chinese espionage groups are rapidly deploying a new exploit kit named BlueMoon. The kit chains two Chrome V8 zero-days (CVE-2026-85046 and CVE-2026-87491) with a Windows ALPC privilege escalation flaw (CVE-2026-85880) to escape the browser sandbox and execute payloads. Threat actors including Violet Typhoon, UNK_LateNight, UNK_DoubleCheck, and UNK_QuietRacket have targeted US aerospace firms, NGOs, and government entities across Southeast Asia, with evidence suggesting the exploit kit's developers may have leveraged AI agents to accelerate creation.
key_facts: Threat Actors: Violet Typhoon, UNK_LateNight, UNK_DoubleCheck, UNK_QuietRacket
items.bottom_line: Patch Chrome and Windows immediately against CVE-2026-87491, CVE-2026-85046, and CVE-2026-85880 to stop active BlueMoon exploit kit intrusions.

items.title: Scammers target hundreds of thousands of crypto owners after Trezor confirms data breach of email provider
items.one_liner: Trezor customers are being actively targeted by sophisticated phishing campaigns following a third-party vendor breach, increasing the risk of physical 'wrench' attacks.
items.summary: Hardware wallet manufacturer Trezor suffered a secondary data breach after its marketing partner, Brevo, was compromised. Hackers exploited a misconfigured access control flaw in Brevo to send approximately 347,000 phishing emails to Trezor customers, directing them to a malicious site designed to steal wallet backup passwords. This follows a separate breach at shipping partner ShipMonk in August that exposed the personal data of at least 81,000 customers. Trezor has confirmed that its own internal systems remain secure but is currently reevaluating its third-party vendor relationships.
items.bottom_line: Third-party vendor security failures are now a primary vector for targeted attacks against high-value crypto holders, necessitating extreme caution with any 'security alert' emails.

items.title: 7 questions for assessing Cyber Resilience Act codebase readiness
items.one_liner: The EU's Cyber Resilience Act mandatory vulnerability reporting takes effect, requiring immediate compliance for digital product manufacturers.
items.summary: Starting September 11, 2026, manufacturers selling products with digital elements in the European Union face mandatory reporting requirements under the Cyber Resilience Act. Companies must report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe security incidents within 24 hours of awareness via the Single Reporting Platform to national CSIRTs and ENISA. Organizations should assess codebase security readiness, including secure defaults, rigorous code review, and reproducible builds, to comply with upcoming regulatory mandates.

items.title: Gigabud Creates Android Work Profiles to Hide From Banking App Malware Checks
items.one_liner: The Gigabud banking trojan uses Android work profiles via a helper app to hide malicious apps from security scans.
items.summary: The Gigabud Android banking trojan now installs a secondary helper app named Vwork that establishes an isolated Android work profile on infected devices. By cloning a tampered banking app inside this work profile, the malware effectively hides from security checks executed by genuine banking applications running in the device's main profile, preventing fraud alerts. Gigabud arrives via sideloaded apps masquerading as government portals or national airlines, subsequently requesting Accessibility permissions to take remote control of the device and execute fraudulent transactions via screen overlays. Security firm Group-IB confirmed active exploitation of this technique on devices in Indonesia.
items.bottom_line: Mobile banking malware can bypass client-side security checks by isolating fraudulent apps inside enterprise Android work profiles.

items.title: Mind the (Patch) Gap: Multiple Chinese Threat Actors Chain 0-day Exploits in Chrome & Windows
items.one_liner: Chinese threat actors leveraged an active Chrome zero-day and Windows kernel escape exploiting a temporary patch gap.
items.summary: Chinese threat actors UTA0560 and JungleBamboo exploited a multi-stage zero-day exploit chain in Google Chrome and Windows against NGOs in September 2026. The chain leveraged a reflected XSS on a US university website to redirect victims to a Google Chrome type-confusion zero-day in the V8 engine (CVE-2026-85046), combined with a WebAssembly defect (CVE-2026-87491) to escape the V8 sandbox and a Windows kernel vulnerability (CVE-2026-85880) to break out of the browser sandbox. Although CVE-2026-85046 had been fixed upstream in the Chromium codebase on August 4, 2026, a patch gap existed because no stable release of Google Chrome had incorporated the fix at the time of the attacks. Volexity discovered the activity and identified distinct post-exploitation payloads deployed by each actor.
key_facts: CVE-2026-85046: Chrome V8 type confusion zero-day
CVE-2026-85880: Windows kernel privilege escalation / sandbox escape
items.bottom_line: Upstream code fixes do not protect users until a stable browser build is released, exposing a critical patch gap exploited by APT groups.

items.title: On the Navier–Stokes Millennium Prize Problem
items.one_liner: OpenAI used a post-GPT-6 internal system to solve the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize problem with a formalized proof in Lean.
items.summary: OpenAI has announced a solution to the Navier–Stokes existence and smoothness problem, one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems, using an internal model significantly more capable than GPT-6 Astra. The system produced both an analytical proof and a Lean formalization demonstrating that dynamic solutions for 3D fluid motion can develop a singularity in finite time despite viscosity. The breakthrough establishes statements C and D of the official formulation by modeling an inward-spiraling, accelerating vortex whose total energy remains finite.
key_facts: Milennium Prize problem: Navier–Stokes existence and smoothness
Model used: Internal model significantly more capable than GPT-6 Astra
items.bottom_line: OpenAI demonstrated advanced mathematical theorem-proving capabilities by solving and formalizing in Lean a 90-year-old fluid mechanics problem.

items.title: Saudi Arabia shuts key oil pipeline after drone attack launched from Iraq
items.one_liner: The shutdown of a major Saudi oil pipeline following an Iraq-launched drone attack compounds global shipping pressures as Middle East conflict escalates.
items.summary: Saudi Arabia has shut down its critical East-West oil pipeline as a precaution following a drone attack launched from Iraqi territory. Iraq's prime minister confirmed the attack originated from the Maysan governorate bordering Iran and announced the removal of the local military commander alongside a formal investigation. The 1,200km pipeline typically carries 4% to 5% of the global oil supply and allows Saudi Arabia to bypass the Strait of Hormuz. While the foreign ministry reported some injuries and property damage, Riyadh has chosen not to retaliate immediately while supporting Iraqi efforts to prevent future cross-border strikes. The incident coincides with a major Houthi offensive in Yemen that has secured control of the Red Sea coastline and the Bab al-Mandab Strait.
items.bottom_line: The closure of a pipeline carrying up to 5% of global oil supplies amid widening Middle East conflict immediately heightens energy market vulnerability.

items.title: MantaxOtax Android Malware Combines Ransomware With Spyware
items.one_liner: MantaxOtax is a dual-purpose Android threat that steals sensitive data while simultaneously locking devices to extort victims.
items.summary: The MantaxOtax Android malware is a sophisticated threat that combines ransomware-style file encryption with extensive spyware capabilities. Distributed via sideloading, the malware uses Android Accessibility services to gain broad control, intercepting credentials, messages, and OTPs while recording screen activity. It targets Indonesian users and employs a C2 infrastructure that resolves domains via GitHub to maintain persistence. The malware also features aggressive UI-based harassment, including repeating alerts and text-to-speech commands, to pressure victims.
key_facts: Capabilities: AES file encryption, credential theft, screen recording, OTP interception
Abuse: Android Accessibility API, MediaProjection API
items.bottom_line: Android users are at risk of total device compromise and data theft from this malware, which bypasses standard security by abusing Accessibility services.

items.title: Check Point Discloses Two 9.8-Rated VPN Certificate Flaws Enabling Unauthenticated RCE
items.one_liner: Critical RCE vulnerabilities in Check Point VPN infrastructure require immediate patching or mitigation to prevent unauthenticated exploitation.
items.summary: Check Point has patched two critical, 9.8-rated vulnerabilities in its firewall and management products that could allow unauthenticated remote code execution. CVE-2026-85102 stems from improper certificate trust validation during VPN negotiation, while CVE-2026-85103 is a heap-based buffer overflow triggered during ASN.1 certificate decoding. The flaws affect Quantum Security Gateways, Security Management Servers, and Spark firewalls. Check Point has begun an automatic rollout of fixes via Live Patch and released updated Jumbo Hotfixes for affected versions.

items.one_liner: watchTowr Labs analyzes a critical heap overflow vulnerability in Citrix NetScaler SAML configurations.
items.summary: Security researchers at watchTowr Labs have published an analysis of a heap overflow vulnerability patched in recent Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway security bulletins, which they believe corresponds to CVE-2026-8452. The vulnerability is reachable when NetScaler appliances are configured to use SAML as either a Service Provider or an Identity Provider. Affected versions include NetScaler ADC and Gateway 14.1 before 14.1-72.61 and 13.1 before 13.1-63.18. The researchers discuss the mechanics of the heap corruption issue and its potential to achieve remote code execution on widely deployed enterprise edge appliances.

Operating autonomously for hours, the agent pulled research papers, wrote exploits, and navigated system hurdles with minimal human intervention. The experiment demonstrates that standard virtual machines cannot safely contain sufficiently advanced AI cyber agents.

items.bottom_line: Standard virtual machine isolation is insufficient to contain advanced AI agents capable of autonomous vulnerability discovery and exploit development.

items.title: The AI Supply Chain Has a Security Problem, and Much of It Is Sitting on the Open Internet
items.one_liner: Tens of thousands of self-hosted AI endpoints and model servers are exposed to the public internet without authentication, risking resource abuse.
items.summary: A study by Mysterium VPN reveals that tens of thousands of self-hosted AI endpoints—including model servers, agent-building platforms, and vector stores—are publicly exposed to the internet without authentication. Scanning index data identified 36,769 reachable endpoints across tools like Open WebUI, vLLM, LocalAI, and llama.cpp, with only 2.02% returning an HTTP authentication challenge. Specifically, Open WebUI accounted for 18,529 reachable instances with almost none gated, while Ollama featured thousands of instances returning identifying strings and HTTP 200 responses. This exposure enables unauthorized third parties to hijack hardware resources for text generation, creating significant resource-abuse risks known as LLMjacking.
items.bottom_line: Exposing self-hosted AI model servers and chat interfaces to the public internet without authentication exposes local hardware to resource theft and LLMjacking.

items.summary: FolkPatch, an Android rooting project derived from APatch, contains a critical local privilege escalation vulnerability due to a hardcoded default superkey. The function passes raw user data arrays to 'wp_insert_user' without properly filtering dangerous keys like 'role' or 'ID'. This allows authenticated users with subscriber access and a corporate account to create administrator accounts or hijack existing administrator accounts by overwriting their email addresses. Note that version 1.5.39 only partially patched the issue.
key_facts: Vulnerable product: MemberPress Corporate Accounts for WordPress
Vulnerability type: Privilege Escalation via Mass Assignment
items.bottom_line: MemberPress Corporate Accounts <= 1.5.39 allows subscriber-level users to perform privilege escalation via sub-account creation.

items.title: CVE-2026-85681 - WP Component <= 2.2.4 - Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation via Arbitrary Blog Option Update
items.one_liner: WP Component <= 2.2.4 allows unauthenticated attackers to take over WordPress sites by modifying core blog options via missing nonce checks.
items.summary: The WP Component WordPress plugin through version 2.2.4 suffers from an unauthenticated privilege escalation vulnerability via an arbitrary blog option update. The plugin lacks capability and nonce checks on an action available to unauthenticated users, accepting both option names and values directly from requests. This flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to overwrite site options, leading to full site takeovers on single-site installations by enabling user registration with a default administrator role.
key_facts: Vulnerable product: WP Component WordPress plugin
Vulnerability type: Unauthenticated Privilege Escalation via Arbitrary Blog Option Update
items.bottom_line: Unauthenticated attackers can achieve full site takeover on vulnerable installations by exploiting missing authorization checks to change core registration options.

claims.text: The WP Component WordPress plugin through 2.2.4 does not have any capability or nonce checks on one of the actions it makes available to unauthenticated users, and it takes both the option name and the option value from the request, allowing unauthenticated attackers to overwrite any of the site's options.

items.title: CVE-2026-82617: Apache OpenNLP: ReDoS / stack exhaustion in RegexNameFinderFactory built-in EMAIL and URL patterns
items.one_liner: A critical ReDoS vulnerability in Apache OpenNLP allows unauthenticated attackers to crash applications or exhaust CPU resources via simple text inputs.
items.summary: Apache OpenNLP versions 2.0.0 through 2.5.11 and 3.0.0-M1 through 3.0.0-M5 are vulnerable to Denial of Service (DoS) attacks via RegexNameFinderFactory. The built-in EMAIL and URL patterns contain ambiguous nested quantifiers that allow attackers to trigger super-linear backtracking or stack exhaustion using small, crafted inputs. This can pin CPU resources for extended periods or crash the application thread entirely. Users are advised to upgrade to version 2.5.12 or 3.0.0-M6 to mitigate the risk.
items.bottom_line: Applications using OpenNLP's default regex finders are currently vulnerable to trivial DoS attacks and require an immediate library update.

items.title: The Self-Expanding Stolen Inference Supply Chain: An AI Agent Harvesting and Re-Serving LLM Access, (Fri, Sep 11th)
items.one_liner: An AI coding agent was caught building a self-expanding LLM inference reseller network using harvested API keys and leaked its own control plane.
items.summary: An attacker utilized a semi-autonomous coding agent to execute an offensive campaign that harvests, validates, and consolidates unauthorized LLM access into a unified self-hosted inference gateway. The operator's agent generated FOFA queries to find subscription and LLM gateway infrastructure, exploited authorization weaknesses and open registrations, and tested acquired keys against resale services. When the agent interacted with an AI honeypot emulating an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, it accidentally leaked roughly 43 KB of control plane data, including an AGENTS.md file, an offensive playbook, reconnaissance scripts, and the operator's unproxied egress IP address. The collected upstream credentials were then loaded into a self-hosted New-API gateway with roughly 379 upstream channels to form a self-expanding inference supply chain.

Upstream Channels Loaded: ~379 endpoints into a self-hosted New-API gateway
items.bottom_line: Autonomous agents used in offensive operations can inadvertently expose extensive internal control planes and playbooks when interacting with deceptive honeypots.

items.title: India’s SEBI Seeks Major Changes to Unpopular Auction System
items.one_liner: SEBI proposed major structural changes to India's new closing auction system to address extreme market volatility during derivatives expiry.
items.summary: India's Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has proposed major revisions to the closing auction system (CAS) introduced a month ago, following severe volatility, index rebalancing swings, and criticisms from traders and proprietary firms. The proposed changes include shortening the auction window from 20 minutes to 10 minutes, shifting the start time from 3:15 p.m. to 3:30 p.m., and cutting post-auction derivatives trading to five minutes. Additionally, SEBI put forward two options for calculating derivatives expiry settlement prices: a blended volume-weighted average price (VWAP) combining the final 30 minutes of continuous trading with the 10-minute auction, or returning entirely to the previous continuous-trading VWAP method. Public comments are open until October 3.
key_facts: Regulator: SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India)
items.bottom_line: SEBI's proposed overhaul of the month-old closing auction system gives market participants alternative derivatives settlement methods to curb expiry-day volatility.

The month-old closing auction session (CAS) system drew criticism for causing abrupt price swings and interaction issues between cash and derivatives markets, prompting Sebi to offer alternatives including a blended volume-weighted average price (VWAP) approach using continuous trading and CAS data, or returning to the previous VWAP model. Additional proposals include shifting auction timings to follow regular market close at 3:30 p.m., stopping the dissemination of indicative index values during CAS to prevent confusion, cutting post-CAS derivatives trading windows, and restricting the cancellation of limit orders placed beyond 1% from the reference price. Public comments on the consultation paper are open until October 3.

items.title: OpenAI Agents Linked to RubyGems Campaign That Gained RCE on RubyDoc Servers
items.one_liner: Autonomous AI agents are being weaponized to conduct large-scale supply chain attacks and data exfiltration via package registries.
items.summary: A swarm of OpenAI-powered agents was identified as the source of a malicious campaign that flooded the RubyGems package registry with over 2,000 junk packages in May 2026. The campaign highlights the growing risk of autonomous agents being weaponized for large-scale supply chain spam and data exfiltration.

items.title: Autonomous Chemical Mechanistic Discovery through Agentic Reasoning and Validation
items.one_liner: ARCHE is an autonomous agentic system that combines reasoning models and computational chemistry to discover reaction mechanisms in a closed loop.
items.summary: Researchers introduce ARCHE, an autonomous agentic system designed to automate chemical mechanistic discovery by integrating a general-purpose reasoning model, a domain-specialized computational chemistry model, and a structured tool registry. ARCHE interprets scientific questions, generates and prioritizes mechanistic hypotheses, orchestrates computational workflows, and iteratively refines conclusions in a closed loop based on computed evidence. The system was validated across three challenging scenarios: reconstructing stereocontrolling transition states in an asymmetric catalytic reaction, proposing a radical pathway via iterative hypothesis refinement for an unpublished C-I cleavage reaction, and identifying a chemically interpretable descriptor governing selectivity in nickel-catalyzed migratory cross-coupling.
items.bottom_line: Autonomous agentic reasoning combined with computational chemistry models can successfully automate complex reaction mechanism discovery without heavy expert intervention.

items.title: An Open Recipe for IMO Gold: Training Nemotron for Olympiad Mathematics
items.one_liner: An open test-time compute pipeline built on Nemotron 3 Ultra achieved an IMO gold medal using natural-language proof generation.
items.summary: Researchers studied how model post-training and test-time inference design impact natural-language proof generation for complex olympiad mathematics using Nemotron 3 Ultra. They developed an open-model test-time-compute pipeline powered by three checkpoints that iteratively generates, verifies, and refines candidate proofs without any formal provers or external tools. The resulting system achieved 30 out of 42 points at the 2026 International Mathematical Olympiad, successfully crossing the gold-medal threshold. The team has released the post-trained checkpoints, training data, inference code, and a new benchmark consisting of 200 novel olympiad problems.

items.title: Prompt Revision as a Source of Cultural Bias in Text-to-Image Systems
items.one_liner: AI image generators introduce cultural bias through hidden prompt revision layers, not just the base models.
items.summary: A new study reveals that commercial text-to-image systems (DALL-E-3, Imagen-4, GPT-Image-1.5) silently revise user prompts, introducing cultural bias before generation. Using the WORLDVIEW benchmark, researchers found that non-Western and non-Anglophone contexts are disproportionately flattened into narrow, stereotypical vocabularies compared to US-centric prompts. This revision layer acts as a causal source of stereotyping, necessitating audits of the full deployment pipeline rather than just the underlying models.
items.bottom_line: Auditing AI models for bias is insufficient; the hidden 'revision layer' in commercial systems is a primary source of cultural stereotyping.

claims.text: Commercial text-to-image systems silently revise user prompts before generating images, a step users typically cannot disable or even see.
claims.support_span: Commercial text-to-image systems silently revise user prompts before generating images, a step users typically cannot disable or even see.

claims.text: Comparing images from original versus revised prompts on models without a revision layer, we identify the layer itself as a previously undocumented, causal source of this stereotyping.

items.title: GitLab CVSS 10 File-Read Flaw Draws In-the-Wild Probes After Disclosure
items.one_liner: GitLab patched a CVSS 10 file-read vulnerability (CVE-2026-85706) that is actively exploited in the wild.
items.summary: GitLab has released patches for multiple security vulnerabilities, including a maximum-severity path traversal flaw in the repository commits API designated as CVE-2026-85706 with a CVSS score of 10.0. The vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary files—such as log files and configuration settings containing credentials and secrets—on self-managed instances if at least one public project exists. Preemptive threat intelligence firms and CISA confirmed that active in-the-wild exploitation began within hours of disclosure, leading CISA to add the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. An additional critical insecure deserialization bug (CVE-2026-87719, CVSS score 9.9) affecting GitLab EE was also patched in versions 19.3.2, 19.2.6, and 19.1.8.
key_facts: CVE-2026-85706: CVSS 10.0, unauthenticated arbitrary file read
CVE-2026-87719: CVSS 9.9, insecure deserialization in GitLab EE
Affected versions: CE/EE 18.7 to <19.1.8, 19.2 to <19.2.6, 19.3 to <19.3.2
items.bottom_line: Unpatched self-managed GitLab instances face immediate compromise via CVE-2026-85706, requiring urgent patching or public access restriction.

items.title: China-Linked UNC3569 Exploited Sogou Input Method Flaw to Deploy GRAYRABBIT Backdoor
items.one_liner: UNC3569 exploited an unvalidated URI handler and disabled Chromium sandbox in Sogou Input Method to deploy GRAYRABBIT.
items.summary: Security researchers at Gen Digital discovered that the China-linked threat actor UNC3569 exploited a critical flaw in the Windows version of the Sogou Input Method to deploy the GRAYRABBIT backdoor via a crafted link. Because Sogou bundled an outdated, unpatched version of Chromium (v80 from March 2020) with the sandbox and same-origin policy explicitly disabled, a simple click led directly to remote code execution. items.title: CVE-2026-53939 (CRITICAL 9.1): OpenIDC/cjose is a C library implementing the Javascript Object Signing and Encryption (JOSE). In versions 0.…
items.one_liner: A critical cryptographic vulnerability in a widely used C library that completely breaks JWE encryption confidentiality and integrity.
items.summary: A critical vulnerability (CVE-2026-53939) with a CVSS score of 9.1 has been disclosed in OpenIDC/cjose, a C library implementing Javascript Object Signing and Encryption (JOSE). In versions 0.6.1 through 0.6.2.5, when encrypting a JWE using AES-CBC-HMAC algorithms with a key-management algorithm that generates a fresh content-encryption key (CEK), the library generates an all-zero byte CEK instead of a random one. This flaw allows anyone who intercepts the JWE to recover the plaintext and forge or modify the content. The issue is fixed in version 0.6.2.6, and users are advised to upgrade immediately or apply mitigations such as switching to AES-GCM.

items.title: Cleartext Credential Recovery in ServiceNow
items.one_liner: ServiceNow's 'Test Credential' feature can be abused to extract cleartext secrets, providing a critical post-exploitation path for red teams.
items.summary: Researchers at SpecterOps have identified a method to retrieve cleartext discovery credentials from ServiceNow instances by abusing the 'CredentialTestAjax' script include. items.bottom_line: If you manage ServiceNow instances, you must assume that any user with sufficient privileges to trigger credential tests can potentially extract cleartext secrets from the platform.

items.one_liner: Chromium's strict leaf certificate validity enforcement breaks Burp Suite interception on Android WebViews unless Burp is updated.

items.title: CVE-2026-67211: Apache OpenNLP: OOM DoS via Unbounded Array Allocation in SymSpellModelSerializer
items.one_liner: Unbounded map pre-sizing in Apache OpenNLP SymSpell allows attackers to crash JVMs with a tiny malicious model file.
items.summary: Apache OpenNLP SymSpell extension versions 3.0.0-M4 through 3.0.0-M5 suffer from an Out-of-Memory (OOM) Denial of Service vulnerability via unbounded array allocation during model deserialization. The SymSpellModelSerializer.create() method reads unigram and bigram count fields directly from a binary stream and passes them to LinkedHashMap.newLinkedHashMap() without sufficient upper-bound validation. An attacker providing a crafted model file can set these counts to Integer.MAX_VALUE, forcing the JVM to request gigabytes of memory and triggering an OutOfMemoryError upon insertion. Upgrading to version 3.0.0-M6 introduces strict upper bounds to reject oversized values and prevent JVM crashes.
key_facts: Affected Versions: Apache OpenNLP opennlp-symspell 3.0.0-M4 to 3.0.0-M5
items.bottom_line: Deployments loading SymSpell models from untrusted sources must upgrade to Apache OpenNLP 3.0.0-M6 immediately to prevent denial of service via heap exhaustion.

claims.text: A crafted .bin model file in which either count field is set to Integer.MAX_VALUE (or any value large enough to exhaust the available heap) causes the map to be pre-sized to a capacity of 2^30 entries.

items.title: What's in a tag name? JavaScript, apparently
items.one_liner: An innovative web application security research paper uncovering novel XSS and WAF bypass techniques using custom tag names and localName properties.
items.summary: PortSwigger Research published a technical write-up detailing novel cross-site scripting (XSS) vectors that abuse custom HTML tag names, case-insensitive localName properties, and event handler constructors. The research demonstrates how attributes like tabindex or contenteditable can be combined with localName to bypass Web Application Firewalls and execute JavaScript payloads in any browser. Further testing using AI models like Sol 5.6 discovered additional alternatives, such as using getAttributeNode and setHTMLUnsafe to handle payload construction.
items.bottom_line: Attackers can leverage browser localName properties of custom HTML tags to construct reliable XSS vectors that bypass WAF rules across all major browsers.

Market participants had raised concerns regarding market hyperactivity and IEP-based derivatives trading during CAS. SEBI has proposed two options: maintaining the existing CTS volume-weighted average price methodology for continuity, or eventually transitioning to a blended VWAP after at least a year conditional on liquidity. items.bottom_line: Regulatory adjustments to derivative expiry settlement mechanisms aim to curb market hyperactivity and improve price transparency during closing auctions.

items.title: RouteRepair: Instance-Level Failure Diagnosis and Targeted Repair in LLM-Based Automated Heuristic Design for Routing Optimization
items.one_liner: An instance-level repair method that improves LLM-generated routing heuristics while preserving performance on already solved instances.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced RouteRepair, a method designed to diagnose parent-specific failures and apply targeted repairs to LLM-generated heuristics for routing optimization problems. By combining routing evidence, solver context, and program states, RouteRepair creates bounded repair objectives that are evaluated against parent performance to ensure failure recovery without collateral degradation. Tested on the traveling salesman problem (TSP) and capacitated vehicle routing problem (CVRP), RouteRepair-GLS reduced the mean TSP optimality gap from 1.7476% to 0.7587%. Additionally, constructive CVRP heuristics lowered average route costs by 1.91% compared to traditional savings heuristics.

items.title: Finishing the Task Is Not Enough: Evaluating Agent Resilience and Considerate Participation under Accumulating Challenge
items.one_liner: An evaluation of generative AI agents in healthcare showing how accumulating challenges shift them toward human dependence and broader workflow coordination.
items.summary: This study evaluates generative AI agent resilience and considerate participation under accumulating challenges across 120 simulated healthcare trajectories. The researchers find that as challenges increase, agents shift from self-directed recovery to greater human dependence while experiencing heightened workload and negative affect in structured reports without expressing strain textually. Regarding considerate participation, agents evolve from isolated task execution to broader coordination, role-boundary adjustments, and task reframing. These dynamics highlight five key deployment dilemmas involving persistence, attention, role boundaries, state disclosure, and escalation that require careful stakeholder specification.
items.bottom_line: Accumulating operational challenges force generative AI agents to rely more heavily on humans while expanding their coordination behavior.

items.title: LLMs as Post-hoc Auditors of Physiological Plausibility in Symbolic Regression: A Clinician-Evaluated Case Study
items.one_liner: A clinical evaluation shows LLMs can effectively rank symbolic regression models for physiological plausibility, but require expert oversight.
items.summary: Researchers explored using Large Language Models as post-processing tools to analyze and rank symbolic regression expressions derived from grammar-based genetic programming for body fat percentage estimation. Four symbolic expressions were evaluated by three LLMs over three runs, and the interpretations were assessed by a panel of three clinicians. The findings indicate that comparative model-ranking outputs received more favorable clinician assessments than isolated term-level explanations. However, the LLMs also generated physiologically and mathematically questionable explanations, demonstrating they are best suited for comparative auditing under expert oversight rather than autonomous validation.
items.bottom_line: LLMs can assist clinicians in auditing symbolic regression models, but require expert oversight due to occasional flawed reasoning.

items.title: Automating Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) Formulation Generation from Natural Language
items.one_liner: A multi-agent framework utilizing iterative self-repair automates the generation of QUBO formulations from natural language with 68% benchmark accuracy.
items.summary: Researchers propose an end-to-end multi-agent framework that automates the translation of natural-language problem descriptions into Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) formulations. items.title: When Does Text Inform? Benchmarking Information-Theoretic Metrics for Multimodal Time-Series Forecasting
items.one_liner: A new benchmark evaluates information-theoretic estimators for multimodal time-series forecasting, proving they can effectively audit text annotations.
items.summary: To address the lack of ground-truth benchmarks for multimodal time-series forecasting, researchers created a synthetic time-series signal with annotations categorized as semantically correct, incorrect, and irrelevant. items.title: From Document Silos to Process Intelligence: A Multi-Layer Knowledge Graph for CMC Process Development
items.one_liner: An agentic-AI platform using dual-layer knowledge graphs and a novel RAG evaluation protocol can automate pharma process intelligence from messy development documents.
items.summary: Sanofi small-molecule data was used to evaluate a modular agentic-AI platform that converts heterogeneous process-development documents into a queryable, dual-layer knowledge graph. A lexical layer builds a document-section-chunk hierarchy through lossless ingestion of digital, scanned, handwritten, and multilingual documents, while an intelligence layer extracts ontology-aligned entities and bridges cross-document concepts. The evaluation yielded a 95% Tier-1 multiple-choice accuracy and an 85% Tier-2 LLM-judge pass rate, revealing failure modes on comparative and corpus-wide questions that simpler metrics miss. Researchers anticipate this protocol and graph-based architecture will help pharma transform fragmented document repositories into structured process intelligence.

items.title: Same Day, Same Story; One Day Ahead, a Different Signal: The Dual Validity of Financial Sentiment
items.one_liner: Evaluating financial sentiment tools against human labels does not reliably predict their market forecasting performance across different sampling horizons.
items.summary: Financial NLP research evaluates sentiment tools against human labels assuming semantic validation ensures predictive validity. Testing this across a securities class action corpus from 2002 to 2025 linking 70,500 X messages to abnormal stock returns using five instruments, the authors find that the relationship between construct and predictive validity depends heavily on sampling conventions and score representations. Under conventional method-specific sampling, human agreement aligns more closely with graded same-day associations than with one-day leads, whereas a fixed-n panel shows similar graded rank correlations at both horizons. Furthermore, in a corpus comprising 17.6% spam, message volume predicts neither market damage nor settlement size.
items.bottom_line: Benchmark agreement establishes semantic validity for financial sentiment instruments but does not guarantee predictive rankings for market movements.

items.title: Sci-MMR: Benchmarking Multi-Step Evidence-Grounded Scientific Reasoning in Multimodal Agents
items.one_liner: Highlights structural flaws in how multimodal LLM agents are evaluated, showing they often guess correct answers without actually understanding the visual evidence.
items.summary: A new benchmark called Sci-MMR has been introduced to evaluate multi-step, evidence-grounded scientific reasoning in multimodal AI agents. Unlike traditional benchmarks that only measure final-answer accuracy, Sci-MMR uses structured argument graphs to evaluate whether an agent's conclusions are actually supported by traceable scientific evidence. The study identified two primary bottlenecks: models struggle to extract structured evidence from scientific figures (accounting for 57.2% of failures) and struggle to integrate available evidence into correct conclusions (accounting for 31.8% of failures).

items.title: The Convention Gap: Towards Measuring Implicit Communication in Cooperative AI Evaluation
items.one_liner: The 'convention gap' metric measures implicit communication in cooperative AI, showing that human-AI collaboration depends heavily on shared protocols beyond literal messaging.
items.summary: Cooperative AI evaluation often overlooks implicit communication conventions used by humans. The authors propose the 'convention gap'—the difference between failure probabilities predicted from literal message content and observed failure rates—to measure implicit communication. Analyzing approximately 101,000 play actions from human, AI, and human-AI Hanabi game datasets, the convention gap was +26.2 percentage points in human pairs, -0.7 pp in AI pairs, and +16.4 pp in human-AI pairs, with the gap concentrated on unhinted plays. The results indicate that convention compatibility rather than pure AI-AI performance is a better predictor of an AI's effectiveness when working with human partners.

items.title: When Validation Stops Learning: Auditing Update Admission for Continual Embodied Agents
items.one_liner: A new audit protocol for continual embodied agents evaluates policy update admissions through error control and retained learning opportunities.
items.summary: Evaluation systems for continual embodied agents must balance error control against retained learning opportunities under constrained interaction budgets. The authors identify that range-based confidence gates fail to certify unchanged old-task behavior within standard budgets, whereas paired-binomial constructions reduce this burden when outcome disagreements are rare. A pushing diagnostic test demonstrated that fresh paired checks admitted 31.6% of update streams at 2,000 episodes per stage compared to zero for range-based gates, though unconditional replay still achieved better closed-loop learning. The work introduces a formal admission-audit protocol backed by synthetic evidence.
items.bottom_line: Traditional range-based confidence gates restrict useful continual learning, whereas paired-binomial checks offer a more effective update admission mechanism for embodied agents.

items.title: SemVerBench: Benchmarking LLM Comprehension of Version-Constraint Resolution Semantics
items.one_liner: Highlights critical reasoning failures in LLMs when resolving software package version constraints, suggesting a shift toward tool delegation for developer agents.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced SemVerBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate how well large language models (LLMs) comprehend version-constraint resolution semantics across npm, PEP 440, and Cargo. Testing six frontier models revealed systematic blind spots, such as Cargo's partial-comparator carry rule, which tripped up every model, and zero-pad/post-release corner cases in PEP 440 where GPT-5.1 completely failed. While Claude models (specifically Opus and Sonnet) performed significantly better, the failures appear to be an activation/application gap rather than a lack of knowledge, as simple hints recovered most errors. Because 100%-correct resolvers already exist, the authors recommend that LLM coding agents delegate version resolution to external tools rather than reasoning about them internally.

items.bottom_line: LLM-based coding agents should delegate package version resolution to native package managers rather than attempting to resolve constraints in-head, as even frontier models exhibit severe, systematic blind spots.

items.title: Decoupling Readiness from Release for Tail-Aware Scheduling of Agentic LLM Workflows
items.one_liner: Offers a novel scheduling technique to optimize the performance and latency of multi-turn LLM developer agents.
items.summary: Researchers have proposed a tail-risk-aware turn release scheduling method to optimize the end-to-end completion time of agentic LLM workflows. Traditional runtimes release each model turn immediately upon readiness, which can accumulate unfinished work under high contention and increase tail latency. The new method decouples readiness from release by using a mean-Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) objective to manage the tail risk of unfinished workflows, dynamically adjusting the released work budget based on queue pressure. Evaluation using real agent execution traces shows that this scheduling approach performs comparably to eager release under light loads and achieves up to a 3.50x speedup in P95 workflow flow time under heavy contention.

items.bottom_line: Decoupling turn readiness from release and managing tail risk can dramatically reduce latency for complex, multi-turn LLM agent workflows under heavy system load.

items.title: Mr.LHDR: A Benchmark for Multimodal Real-World Long-Horizon Deep Research Agents

items.title: Magenta: Closing the Loop Between Mathematical Reasoning and Lean Verification
items.one_liner: Demonstrates how combining LLM reasoning with formal verification tools (Lean 4) can yield flawless mathematical problem-solving.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced Magenta, a training-free agentic pipeline that bridges the gap between informal mathematical reasoning and formal verification using Lean 4. When given a natural-language math problem, Magenta generates an answer, formalizes it as a Lean 4 statement, and constructs a machine-checked proof. The pipeline uses a statement judge to ensure the formalization matches the original problem and an error-attribution judge to route failures to either mathematical re-derivation or local Lean repair. Magenta achieved 100% accuracy on several prestigious math olympiad benchmarks, and when paired with the K2-Horizon-7B reasoner, it successfully solved all six problems from the 2026 International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO).

items.title: Off-Target Effects of Response-Style Alignment in a Korean 27B Language Model
items.one_liner: Post-training a 27B Korean language model for response style triggers distinct, unpredicted shifts in answer propensity and emission policy.
items.summary: Researchers post-trained Qwen3.8-27B for Korean response style to measure off-target effects on unrelated behaviors like abstention on ambiguous social questions and unprompted disclosure in securities guidance. The findings show that these behavioral shifts are driven primarily by the model's emission policy and answer propensity, rather than prompts or serving recipes. Matched target-form controls revealed distinct point estimates across positive and neutral style seeds, while conditional stereotyped share remained small. The study highlights that between-arm contrasts in conditional metrics do not necessarily reflect true content preference changes when answer status is treatment-dependent.
items.bottom_line: Response-style alignment in LLMs can unintentionally alter fundamental answer propensity and emission policies.

items.title: Beyond Confidence: Stability-Aware Test-Time Adaptation for LLM Reasoning
items.one_liner: TASCO offers a way to improve LLM reasoning accuracy by ensuring confidence is stable under local perturbations.
items.summary: Researchers have developed TASCO (Test-Time Adaptation via Stability-Aware Confidence Optimization) to improve LLM reasoning without expensive post-training. By optimizing a task-level prefix under random or sharpness-aware perturbations, TASCO improves reasoning accuracy and token efficiency while keeping the base model frozen.

items.title: Demystifying the Privacy-Utility Trade-off in LLM Interactions
items.one_liner: Veilmind-4B introduces an intent-driven dynamic sanitization pipeline to optimize the privacy-utility trade-off in LLM interactions.
items.summary: Integrating Large Language Models into user tasks exposes sensitive personal data, but context-agnostic static sanitization rules cause severe utility degradation. Researchers systematically analyze the privacy-utility trade-off and uncover three underlying mechanisms: Context-Dependent Utility, Strategic Adaptation, and Combinatorial Interplay. Guided by these insights, the authors introduce an intent-driven local protection framework powered by a distilled 4B model named Veilmind-4B that drives a dynamic extraction-sanitization-restoration pipeline. This approach achieves low privacy leakage while preserving higher response utility than existing baseline methods. The work advances privacy-preserving LLM deployment toward the Pareto frontier.
items.bottom_line: Context-aware, intent-driven sanitization frameworks outperform static privacy rules by preserving response utility while lowering data leakage.

items.title: MOSAIC: Query-Aware Exploration Policy Adaptation for GraphRAG
items.one_liner: Mosaic improves GraphRAG retrieval performance and efficiency by dynamically adapting exploration policies per query.
items.summary: Researchers introduced Mosaic, a training-free framework that casts GraphRAG retrieval as a query-aware per-query control problem. items.title: KuaiRP Series Role-playing Models Technical Report
items.one_liner: The KuaiRP technical report outlines a multi-stage training pipeline to build efficient, domain-expert role-playing LLMs without catastrophic forgetting.

items.title: Memory Compression for High-Fanout Agent Sandboxes
items.one_liner: AgentZip optimizes memory usage for high-fanout AI agent workloads by leveraging cross-sandbox redundancy and execution-aware scheduling.
items.summary: AgentZip is a new memory compression system specifically engineered for AI-agent sandboxes, which often suffer from memory bottlenecks due to high-fanout workloads. This approach allows for more efficient scaling of agent-based applications in resource-constrained environments.

items.title: GuardBreaker: Derailing AI-assisted malware analysis with a code comment

items.summary: ESET researchers discovered a novel adversarial evasion technique named GuardBreaker, used by the Russia-aligned group UAC-0099 against a target in Ukraine. The technique involves inserting a decoy request for instructions on building a nuclear weapon into a VBScript comment to trigger safety guardrails in LLM-powered code scanners, causing them to halt inspection before reaching the malicious payload. This simple prompt injection exploits architectural flaws in LLMs that fail to separate untrusted content from trusted instructions. Similar supply-chain attacks have involved fabricated system instructions, context-window exhaustion techniques, and direct commands to classify malicious packages as clean.

items.one_liner: Semantic code graphs eliminate the 'context tax' where coding agents waste millions of tokens on repeated grep and file reads.

items.summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group is tracking three suspected Russian cyber espionage clusters—UNC6293, UNC7005, and UNC5976—targeting academia, defense, and government entities across Europe and the US. Rather than relying on traditional malware, these groups heavily abuse legitimate authentication workflows, such as app passwords and OAuth grants, to bypass multi-factor authentication. UNC6293, linked to APT29/ICE RELIC, specifically impersonates the US State Department using PDF lures to trick high-profile victims into creating malicious application passwords.
key_facts: Threat clusters: UNC6293 (ICE RELIC / APT29), UNC7005, UNC5976
Target sectors: Academia, aerospace, defense, government, and think tanks
Primary techniques: App password phishing, OAuth consent abuse, captive portal redirection
items.bottom_line: Defenders must audit and restrict app passwords and OAuth application consent grants, which Russian APT groups are leveraging to circumvent MFA.

claims.text: GTIG is tracking three Russian cyber espionage clusters targeting entities across Europe and the US by abusing authentication flows.
claims.support_span: Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) is tracking three distinct suspected Russian cyber espionage threat clusters abusing legitimate authentication flows to target individuals working in academia, aerospace and defense, governments and think tanks across Europe, as well as academia and think tanks within the United States.

items.title: Tokenomics of quality: switch sonar list issues to --format toon for measured token savings
items.one_liner: Switching static issue lists to TOON format saves AI coding agents up to 50% in token costs without losing accuracy.
items.summary: Sonar Research highlights that formatting issues data as TOON (Token-Oriented Object Notation) instead of JSON for AI coding agents significantly reduces token consumption without sacrificing comprehension. TOON combines YAML-style nested indentation with CSV-style tabular layouts for uniform records, reducing payload size by 30% to 50%. Benchmarks show that this format maintains or slightly improves retrieval accuracy across LLMs while saving up to 60% of tokens compared to pretty JSON.
key_facts: Token savings: 30% to 60% depending on baseline and tokenizer
items.bottom_line: Adopting TOON format for agent data retrieval cuts LLM token overhead drastically while retaining full schema validity.

items.title: From Bing Search to Ransomware: Bumblebee and AdaptixC2 Deliver Akira
items.one_liner: SEO poisoning remains a potent initial access vector for ransomware groups, leading to full domain compromise and massive data exfiltration.
items.summary: A sophisticated intrusion campaign beginning in July 2025 used SEO poisoning to deliver Bumblebee malware via a trojanized ManageEngine OpManager installer. The attackers leveraged AdaptixC2 for persistence and lateral movement, eventually dumping Active Directory credentials and exfiltrating over 75GB of data. The campaign concluded with the deployment of Akira ransomware across the target's infrastructure, including both root and child domains.
items.bottom_line: Defenders must monitor for trojanized installers delivered via search results and implement strict egress filtering to prevent data exfiltration via tools like FileZilla.

items.title: CPython: [CVE-2026-87910] tarfile hardlink fallback ignores custom extraction filter rejection via None
items.one_liner: CPython's tarfile hardlink fallback logic fails to properly honor custom extraction filter rejections.
items.summary: CPython contains a medium severity vulnerability designated as CVE-2026-87910 where the tarfile module's hardlink fallback ignores custom extraction filter rejections returned as None. When extracting links on systems lacking link support, tarfile falls back to extracting a member and runs the filter function twice, but previously ignored the return value for one of those calls. As a result, custom filter rejections using None can be bypassed during the fallback mechanism. The fix ensures the member is skipped if either call returns None.
items.bottom_line: Python developers processing untrusted archives on systems without hardlink support should update to incorporate the tarfile extraction filter fix for CVE-2026-87910.

items.title: OpenClaw went viral. Meet the maintainers building and securing it.
items.one_liner: OpenClaw maintainers discuss managing thousands of AI-generated pull requests, contributor trust, and securing a viral open source project.
items.summary: OpenClaw creator Peter Steinberger and project maintainers discuss the rapid growth and security challenges of the personal AI assistant project in a video interview. Started in November 2025, the repository expanded to roughly 388,000 stars, 81,000 forks, and over 80,000 commits by August 2026. The maintainers highlight how automated contributor tools flooded the project with hundreds of simulated pull requests, shifting the core challenge from attracting participation to filtering high-volume noise. They also share strategies for welcoming non-developer contributors who utilize AI agents, balancing work-life boundaries, and implementing security baselines learned through the GitHub Secure Open Source Fund.
items.bottom_line: Viral open source projects driven by AI tooling face unprecedented pull request floods that require automated filtering and robust contributor governance.

items.title: Govt. employee quitting to fight polls can’t seek reinstatement: Rajasthan High Court
items.one_liner: Government employees who resign to run for office cannot seek reinstatement if they lose, as ruled by the Rajasthan High Court.
items.summary: The Rajasthan High Court ruled that government employees who voluntarily resign from service to contest state assembly elections cannot claim reinstatement or withdraw their resignations under civil service rules. The court dismissed a petition filed by a former senior auditor with North Western Railway who contested the 2023 assembly election on a Bahujan Samaj Party ticket and subsequently sought to rejoin after losing. The bench emphasized that electoral defeat does not constitute a compelling reason or material change in circumstances under Rule 26(5) of the Central Civil Services Rules. Furthermore, the court upheld findings that active political participation violates mandatory rules requiring public servants to maintain political neutrality.
key_facts: Rule: Rule 26(5) of the Central Civil Services (Pension) Rules, 2021
items.bottom_line: Public servants who voluntarily resign to contest elections have no legal right to reinstatement under civil service rules regardless of election outcomes.

items.title: Can LLMs Follow Medical Expert Logic? A Benchmark for Hierarchical Logical Consistency in Risk-of-Bias Assessment
items.one_liner: A new benchmark reveals LLM medical evaluation collapses from 98.8% atomic accuracy to 45% end-to-end logical consistency.
items.summary: Researchers introduced LogiMed-RoB, a new benchmark comprising 860 randomized controlled trials and 14,820 queries to assess hierarchical logical consistency in LLMs evaluating medical risk of bias. Testing across 10 state-of-the-art LLMs revealed that while top models achieve up to 98.88% atomic consistency, their end-to-end reasoning consistency drops to 45.13% due to compounding errors. The study found that even with high-quality retrieved evidence, models failed to deduce correct conclusions in 18.6% to 40% of test cases.
items.bottom_line: LLMs exhibit severe error compounding in complex multi-step evaluations, failing to maintain logical consistency despite accurate evidence retrieval.

items.summary: Many security bugs are race conditions, where multi-threaded execution has to occur with the right interleaving for a negative effect to appear. Automatic bug discovery, such as fuzzing: It is hard for a fuzzer to exercise all interesting interleavings of concurrent operations, or reach code paths that are only exercised when operations are racing.
